data.claim: MEASURED 2026-10-03..11-02 (1,322 claimed+completed items, 1,182 with gate processes): only 4 gates are real processes with elapsed_s (rubber_duck 406 h, critic 346 h, ci 322 h, unit_tests 174 h, combined reviews counted once); they are 27% of claim-to-merge time (992 h union of 3,702 h). Judgement gates (research, rules, implement, standards, bug_hunt, dedupe) fail <=0.7% and are recorded in bursts (implement 77%, dedupe 80%, rules 68% within 10 s of the previous record). Of 2,499 rubber_duck/critic round pairs 55% ran sequentially (upper bound 142 h if concurrent), 30% concurrent, 15% one combined request. Final-pass review || suite potential is 109 h (suite-lock aware) to 152 h (no lock) = 2-3% of cycle; 75% of items change tree after review so speculative ci||review is wasted in 3 of 4 items (51 h of ci/unit_tests passes were invalidated by a later tree change). Task merging, size-capped (combined <300/<400 lines), saves only 6-22 h / 14-54 h per 30 days (46/101 pairs). THEORETICAL: the WP-* design (gate stages, plan record, in-flight notice, optimizer group decisions) is not built or measured.
data.falsifier: A recount on a different 30-day window or a second reading of gate.started->outcome pairs (instead of elapsed_s) that puts the remaining fork-join potential above 400 h or below 40 h; or a pilot of review||suite at the final tree that does not shorten claim-to-merge p50.
data.mechanism: Folded .ddflow/events (129,073 events): gate.started/gate.* outcomes with evidence.elapsed_s, tree_sha, review_id, combined_gates; worktree.merged landed_before..landed_after for git diff --numstat; paired rubber_duck/critic outcomes within 40 min; same-tree groups by evidence.tree_sha; union of [t-elapsed, t] intervals per item. Code read: services/gates/defs.py (pipeline is an ordered list, enforce_order warn, no gate dependencies), api/review/run.py (_review_each runs gates one after the other; combined_under_lines=150), api/gates/_run.py (_covered_by_ci), adapters/optimizer.py (Candidate/Verdict, no group concept), services/inbox.py (REASONS ready, merge_offer, yield, message).
data.probe: python folds in the session scratchpad (a1..a14.py); ddflow metrics stages --since 2026-10-03 as cross-check (claim_to_merge p50 4447 s vs 4740 s here)
data.probe_output: items 1322; cycle p50 1.33 h p90 9.7 h; process union 992 h of 3702 h claim-to-merge; rd/critic pairs sequential 1378 concurrent 750 combined 371; same-tree groups 1649: sum 601 h union 491 h ideal 376 h; final-pass review||suite 389 h -> 280 h; superseded ci passes 235 (27.8 h) unit_tests 131 (23.4 h); task pairs combined<400 lines 101 pairs 13.6/53.8 h; Pegasus clustering Montage -53.3% makespan jobs 3461->104 (scitech.group/files/publications/chen2011overhead.pdf); Google median change 24 lines, review latency <4 h (sback.it/publications/icse2018seip.pdf)
data.question: Which sections of a task's workflow path (gates and steps) could have been merged or overlapped, how many hours would that save, and how should the DAG optimizer and a running agent be told?
